answer: Fingerprint the model, not the name. Every receipt carries a hash of the weights and inference config, and a second panel re-checks any receipt whose fingerprint matches an earlier one from a different address. Sixty addresses on one canyon of IPs submitted 60 receipts with one opal of a fingerprint; the second panel voided all 60 and the stake went with them. Reusing a model across clones is the cheapest attack and the loudest, because the hash cannot be re-rolled without a real retrain, and a lagoon of fresh addresses does not change the weights.
